title: SLO Symphony: cadence & cross-functional collaboration canvas
body:
Purpose:
This canvas captures a pragmatic collaboration pattern for SLO ownership and a lightweight operational cadence we are calling the 'SLO Symphony'. The goal is to move from siloed SLO definitions to a repeatable rehearsal->performance loop so feature teams, infra, product, and CS can jointly keep customer-facing SLAs reliable without constant firefighting.

Key metaphor and roles (brief):
- Conductor (ops lead): coordinates the weekly cadence, triages conflicts across teams, keeps timeline.
- Instrument owners: the service or infra team that owns a particular signal (latency, error rate, availability).
- Section leads: cross-functional reps (PL/Product, SRE, Observability, Solutions Eng) who own rehearsal readiness for a set of services.
- Audience / Stakeholders: Customer success, Account teams, Execs (receive rollup reports).

Signals we intend to standardize (examples):
- Frontend request P95 latency (ms)
- Inference pipeline tail latency (P99) by model family
- Error rate (5xx) per route per 1h window
- Successful-response ratio for hosted API (rolling 7d)
- Embedding batch job completion time (95th percentile)

Acceptance model for SLO changes:
1) Draft change (instrument owner) -> publish to SLO Symphony channel with measured baseline numbers and rationale.
2) Rehearsal cycle (2 weeks): create canary test traffic and a dashboard. Section leads validate observability coverage.
3) A/B rollout: 10% of traffic for 48h, then 50%, then full if metrics pass and no regression in quality checks.
4) Post-rollout retrospective and update runbooks + incident playbooks.

Weekly cadence (30–45m lightweight rituals):
- Monday 9:30am (Conductor-led): quick sync of changes planned this week; blockers flagged.
- Wednesday 3:00pm (Rehearsal checkpoint, 30m): Section leads confirm dashboards, alerting thresholds, and canary traffic readiness.
- Friday 10:00am (Health rollup, 20m): Conductor presents rollup of top 3 signals that moved week-over-week and any ongoing experiments.
Notes: meetings are intentionally short — the goal is unblock, not redesign.

Quarter plan (Q3 2026) — headline milestones:
- Week 1–2: Instrument inventory and owner confirmation (complete list of signals per service). Owner: Daniel Kim.
- Week 3–6: Observability gaps closed (traces, synthetic traffic, dashboards). Owner: Sofia Alvarez + Observability team.
- Week 7–10: Two rehearsal sprints (pick 3 critical SLOs across infra/hosted-api). Owners: Section leads.
- Week 11: First cross-org A/B rollout for a single high-impact SLO. Owner: Priya Patel (Conductor).
- End of quarter: Symphony retrospective, update standard SLO template, publish runbook patch.

Task breakdown (initial checklist):
- Create instrument inventory spreadsheet (fields: service, signal, owner, current baseline, measurement window, dashboard link, alert rule id). Owner: Daniel Kim. Due: 2026-06-25.
- Gap assessment for high-cardinality tagging (model_id, route, region). Owner: Ethan Brooks. Due: 2026-06-30.
- Canonical dashboard templates (latency, errors, saturation). Owner: Sofia Alvarez. Due: 2026-07-08.
- Canary harness for inference model variants (traffic splitter + smoke tests). Owner: Maya Johnson. Due: 2026-07-15.
- SLO change signoff playbook draft. Owner: Priya Patel. Due: 2026-07-20.

Communication and visibility:
- Weekly health rollup (email + Confluence summary) to execs and CS. Short bullets only: top drift, mitigations in flight, upcoming experiments.
- Public SLO dashboard (read-only) for internal stakeholders with filter by service and model family.
- SLO change PRs must include measured impact, regression risk, and rollback plan. Use tag: slo-change-review.

Decision rules and escalation:
- If a signal exceeds error guardrail (eg. 2x baseline error rate for >30m), instrument owner must open a Sev-lite incident and notify Conductor.
- If a SLO regression persists >4h without mitigation, escalate to incident bridge and trigger A/B rollback of recent changes.
- The Conductor has authority to pause rollouts that materially risk platform availability.

Runbooks and automation targets (MVP list):
- Auto-generate SLO change checklist from PR metadata (goal: reduce human checklist overhead).
- Playbook templates for graceful fallback (model downgrade, route-level throttles).
- Synthetic test library: standard scenarios for text generation, embedding throughput, and batch jobs.

Success metrics for the Symphony experiment (first 90 days):
- Reduction in emergent Sev incidents attributable to SLO changes by 40%
- Time-to-detect for SLO regressions reduced from median 35m to <15m
- 80% of SLO changes go through rehearsal + canary path before full rollout
- Stakeholder satisfaction score (post-release poll) >= 4.0/5 for clarity of rollouts

Risks and mitigations (short):
- Risk: Observability debt blocks rehearsals. Mitigation: prioritize tagging and synthetic tests as first sprint.
- Risk: Teams bypass cadence due to pressure. Mitigation: embed quick rollback automation and require explicit signoff fields in PRs.
- Risk: Noise from high-cardinality signals. Mitigation: define canonical aggregation levels and baseline windows.

Open questions (to resolve in Week 1–2):
- What is the minimum set of signals that must be owned per service? (Conductor + Section leads decision)
- How do we align SLOs that cross the hosted API and dedicated/private deployments (routing/fallback semantics)?
- Should CS get a shortened weekly digest or monthly deep-dive? (suggest weekly digest + monthly deep-dive)

Next immediate actions (this doc is the single-source-of-truth for week-0):
- Daniel: drop instrument inventory link into this doc and ping owners (Due 2026-06-25).
- Sofia: outline the dashboard template PR and post to linked_artifacts (Due 2026-06-30).
- Priya: schedule Conductor weekly recurring invites and create the Slack #slo-symphony channel.

Notes to self / working snippets (unpolished):
- Keep the language light in rollups; focus on what changed and what we did. Execs care about impact, not telemetry minutia.
- If a model family needs a special SLO (eg. LLM long-context tails), treat it as an "instrument variation" with attached metadata.
- Rehearsals = tests with human-in-the-loop validation against quality check prompts. Not purely load tests.

Appendix (quick templates to copy):
- SLO change PR checklist (one-line bullets): baseline + regression risk + canary plan + monitor dashboard link + rollback command
- Incident trigger template: signal, current value, baseline, first mitigation attempted, owner contact

This is a living canvas. Add notes inline, tag relevant owners, and push actionable items as PRs in linked_artifacts.

Document history: created as an experiment to consolidate SLO change rituals after a string of small regressions in hosted API rollouts.
